page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the server.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25%, whereas the multi-core CPU performance and overall PassMark CPU score fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, though small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels. However, database-related benchmarks show limitations, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations scoring in the bottom 25%, and static web serving throughput ranking in the bottom 10%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and dedicated CPU allocation, this server offers a resource-dense profile for memory-bound tasks that do not require massive parallel processing. The inclusion of 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides a solid storage foundation without requiring external attachments. Due to its weak multi-core and database performance, it is less suited for high-throughput web serving or heavy database workloads. Instead, it is best fit for memory-intensive single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, or small-scale text processing and LLM text generation using small models.
